bundle.author: jagoda
bundle.title: Add the Bifrost gateway's ECS cluster, task and service (phase 1 item 8)
bundle.body:
Phase 1 item 8 of `docs/bifrost-gateway.md`, which is ticked in this PR.

## What this adds

`deploy-workbench/ecs.ts`, wired into `deploy-workbench/index.ts`:

- one `aws.ecs.Cluster` with container insights;
- one Fargate task definition — `awsvpc`, 0.5 vCPU / 1 GB (the plan's sizing),
  x86_64 because the mirror pulls `linux/amd64` — running the Bifrost container
  on 8080;
- one `aws.ecs.Service`, `desiredCount: 1` (OSS Bifrost is single-node, so one
  task is the topology rather than a starting point), in item 5's private
  subnets with item 5's task security group;
- the `/aws/ecs/bifrost` log group at 30 days;
- an execution role with `AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy` plus
  `secretsmanager:GetSecretValue` on `bifrost/gateway`,
  `bifrost/oauth2-proxy` and the RDS-managed master secret;
- a separate task role with no managed policies at all, holding
  `bedrock:Converse`, `bedrock:ConverseStream`, `bedrock:InvokeModel` and
  `bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream` on `bedrockInvokeResources()` from
  `utils/bedrock-models.ts`, and nothing else.

The service does **not** yet name a target group; see "Registering the service"
below for why that cannot happen until item 9.

`ecs.test.ts` pins what would break silently in an apply: the role split, the
secret references by name and JSON key, `initProcessEnabled`, the `awslogs`
configuration, the private-subnet and task-security-group wiring, the
single-task service, the absence of a load-balancer attachment before a
listener references one, the log group name being resolved through
`pulumi.all` rather than read inside `apply`, and that no wildcard IAM action
or `Resource: "*"` is reachable from either role.

## Where it diverges from `deploy/components/worker.ts`

The idiom is copied — `secrets` from Secrets Manager, `awslogs`,
`linuxParameters.initProcessEnabled` — and the divergences are marked `DIFFERS:`
in the module. In sum:

- **The task role is narrow.** The delegate's task role carries five
  AWS-managed read policies and wildcard resources because the delegate is a
  general-purpose agent expected to explore the account. The gateway is a
  proxy: 4 invoke actions, the model ARNs, no `bedrock:*`, no `Resource: "*"`.
- **The execution role reads three secrets, not one.** The delegate's role
  grants read on one Pulumi-owned secret by its exact ARN. Two of these three
  are script-owned, so the grant is a `-??????` name pattern; the third is the
  ARN item 7 returns.
- **One container, not two.** The `oauth2-proxy` sidecar is item 9, and
  registering a container whose image and secrets do not exist yet would be a
  task that cannot start.
- No review bucket, no metric filters, no `AGENT_VERSION`; `AWS_REGION` instead
  of `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`; `cpu`/`memory` follow the constants so the task and
  the container cannot disagree.

## Registering the service

ECS's `CreateService` rejects a target group that no listener or listener rule
references — `InvalidParameterException: The target group with targetGroupArn
... does not have an associated load balancer` — and item 6 attaches neither
group to a routing rule: the HTTPS listener's default action points at
oauth2-proxy, deliberately fail-closed. So item 8 cannot register against
either group, and the plan's "registered against both ALB target groups"
cannot hold until the rules exist. The association and the attachment
therefore arrive together in item 9, with the rules.

Until then the task runs with no target registered, which is the safe
direction: the ALB's default action answers 503, the admin surface is not
reachable, and a container cannot fail a health check nobody is asking for.
`ingress.ts`'s note that item 8 registers a target into the Bifrost group
predates this constraint; correcting it is item 9's, since that item owns the
routing.

## Secrets: referenced, never owned and never read

The two containers are script-owned and already hold real values. Nothing here
declares an `aws.secretsmanager.Secret` or a `SecretVersion`, so nothing can
replace one and delete its contents. The task definition references them by the
names and JSON keys `bifrost/fill-secrets.sh` writes — `bifrost/gateway`'s four
into the Bifrost container — so neither side has to be renamed.

Nor is anything read from Secrets Manager: not a value and not the metadata.
The key list is declared in the repo, as `deploy/delegate-secret.ts` does for
`DELEGATES`, and the ARNs are constructed from the account id, region and name.
`pulumi preview` therefore needs no `secretsmanager` permission at all, which
matters here because the workbench preview role deliberately holds none.

A consequence worth naming: `valueFrom` uses a *partial* ARN, because the six
random characters Secrets Manager appends are unknowable without a describe.
Secrets Manager resolves a partial ARN by name in the same account and region,
which is where this task runs, and it also means a refill of the same secret
does not need a task-definition change.

## What item 8 deliberately does not do

- **No `BIFROST_CONFIG`, no runtime configuration, no provider config.** That is
  item 10. The gateway therefore cannot answer `/health` honestly yet, though
  with no target registered nothing is failing it. This is the plan's staging,
  not a defect, and no configuration was invented to make it green.
- **No oauth2-proxy sidecar and no `OAUTH2_PROXY_*` injection.** That is item 9.
  The secret name, its three keys and the execution role's read grant on it are
  in place so item 9 is a task-definition and listener change rather than an IAM
  change too; nothing in this PR passes one of those keys to a container.
- **No target group, listener, ALB or security group.** All four already exist
  in items 5 and 6, and a second copy would be a target nothing routes to.
- No database, network or DNS change; items 5–7 are consumed as exported.

## Where the plan and the merged code disagreed

- The plan says the service is "registered against both ALB target groups".
  ECS refuses an unassociated target group, and neither group carries a routing
  rule until item 9, so no attachment is possible yet — see "Registering the
  service". Item 9 adds both.
- The plan's item 8 gives the execution role read on "the gateway secret".
  Item 7's module hands this item the RDS-managed master secret to inject as
  `PG_PASSWORD`, and the item 11 script has two containers, so it is three
  ARNs. Only `PG_PASSWORD` is taken from the RDS secret; host, port, user and
  database name are `config.json`'s `env.` references in item 10.
- `deploy-workbench/bifrost/fill-secrets.sh` still describes the containers as
  "the ones phase 2 item 11 creates (Pulumi owns the containers and the read
  grants)". That is stale against the decision that the script owns them. Left
  untouched here to keep this PR to item 8; it is a comment-only fix in a file
  someone else may be editing.

## What item 9 needs from this one

`createBifrostEcs` returns the task definition, the service and the cluster.
Item 9 adds:

- the listener rules, which are what associate both target groups with the ALB;
- the service's `loadBalancers` entries — **both** of them, since item 8 could
  add neither — using `ingress.bifrostTargetGroup`/`ingress.oauth2ProxyTargetGroup`
  and the `BIFROST_CONTAINER_NAME`/`BIFROST_PORT` constants that already exist;
- the `oauth2-proxy` container on 4180, with
  `secretReference(OAUTH2_PROXY_SECRET_NAME, key)` over `OAUTH2_PROXY_SECRET_KEYS`
  (the name, the keys and the read grant already exist) and the
  `oauth2ProxyRepositoryUrl` image `index.ts` already exports;
- the all-three-or-none check on the `OAUTH2_PROXY_*` set, which
  `fill-secrets.sh --check` already reports;
- and it should correct `ingress.ts`'s note about item 8 registering a target.

---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Introduces live ECS/IAM and secret injection for a network-facing gateway, but permissions are narrowly scoped, secrets are not Pulumi-owned, and ALB attachment is intentionally deferred to item 9.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **phase 1 item 8** compute for the Bifrost gateway: new `deploy-workbench/ecs.ts` defines an ECS cluster (container insights), a single **Fargate** task (512 CPU / 1024 MB, x86_64, pinned mirror tag), CloudWatch log group `/aws/ecs/bifrost`, and a **split IAM model**—execution role with ECS execution policy plus read on gateway/oauth2-proxy/RDS secrets; task role with only Bedrock invoke actions on `bedrockInvokeResources()`.
> 
> The Bifrost container gets gateway secrets and `PG_PASSWORD` from RDS via `valueFrom`; secrets are **referenced by name/key** (aligned with `fill-secrets.sh`), not created or read in Pulumi. The service runs in **private subnets** with the existing task security group and **no `loadBalancers` block** until item 9 (ECS rejects unassociated target groups).
> 
> `index.ts` calls `createBifrostEcs` and exports task family and log group name. **`ecs.test.ts`** pins role split, secret wiring, no wildcards, no premature ingress coupling, and `pulumi.all` for log group resolution. **`docs/bifrost-gateway.md`** marks item 8 done and documents deferred ALB registration.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit a44db50839d121a5d3c90447e20732e712c29e36. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

findings.body:
The ECS service has no `deploymentConfiguration` block. ECS Fargate defaults to `minimumHealthyPercent: 100` and `maximumPercent: 200`, which for `desiredCount: 1` means every rolling update starts a second task before stopping the first — transiently running two Bifrost OSS instances against the same Postgres. The plan's "One node, because OSS is one node" section in `docs/bifrost-gateway.md` explicitly states multi-node OSS is **not supported**: it keeps provider configs, keys, budgets and usage in memory and does not re-read them from Postgres. Two simultaneous instances will have divergent in-memory state. The correct deployment strategy for a single-instance stateful service is stop-before-start: `minimumHealthyPercent: 0, maximumPercent: 100`.

(Falsification check: grep confirms no `deploymentConfiguration`, `maximumPercent`, or `minimumHealthyPercent` exists anywhere in the codebase; the plan explicitly prohibits multi-node OSS as unsupported, not merely discouraged. The `deploy/components/worker.ts` idiom omits it too, but that component dispatches ephemeral tasks rather than running a persistent service, so the default is harmless there.)

The "no wildcard IAM action or resource" test builds the execution policy with only one ARN (`secretArnPattern(GATEWAY_SECRET_NAME)`) instead of the real three-ARN shape used in `ecs.ts` (gateway pattern, oauth2-proxy pattern, and the raw RDS ARN). The regex assertion at lines 231–238 — matching `-??????` — would fail for the RDS ARN, which has no such suffix. As written, the test never exercises the no-wildcard property for the RDS secret ARN: if `databaseSecretArn` were accidentally broadened to a wildcard resource, this test would still pass. Consider building the test policy with all three ARN shapes and adjusting the regex loop to accept both `-??????` patterns and exact RDS ARNs.

(Falsification check: no other test in this file asserts `notEqual(resource, "*")` against the three-resource policy shape; the separate test at lines 158–187 checks only action prefixes, not resource shapes.)

output.summary: This PR adds phase 1 item 8 of the Bifrost gateway: an ECS cluster, Fargate task definition (0.5 vCPU / 1 GB, x86_64), single-task service, CloudWatch log group, and split IAM roles (execution role for ECR/logs/secrets, task role for Bedrock invoke only) in `deploy-workbench/ecs.ts`, wired through `index.ts`. The implementation matches the PR description — secrets are referenced by name/key without Pulumi ownership, no load-balancer attachment (deferred to item 9), no runtime config (item 10), and IAM is narrowly scoped with no wildcards. The scout flagged six areas; deep review falsified four (the `/` in secret names is safe for ECS `valueFrom`, the empty-account Bedrock foundation-model ARN is standard AWS format, the extra `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`/`OPENAI_API_KEY` in `fill-secrets.sh` are intentionally optional, and the `resourceBlock()` test helper's EOF capture does not cause false positives). Two findings survived: the ECS service lacks a `deploymentConfiguration` to prevent two simultaneous tasks during rolling updates (a real correctness issue given OSS Bifrost's documented single-node constraint), and the no-wildcard test doesn't exercise the actual three-ARN policy shape including the RDS secret. A human reviewer should confirm whether the `minimumHealthyPercent: 0` brief-downtime tradeoff is acceptable for this service's availability requirements.
